Transnet Pensioners die of poverty as they wait for their day in court

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
This is a fight that has been going on since 2003 and it’s a fight by the oldest and arguably weakest members of society- some 80 000 Transnet Pensioners. Many worked all their lives for the company and believed their old age was secure as the pension fund was arguably one of the strongest at the time. But it got plundered by the State, funds borrowed and not returned, bonds not repaid and since 2003 their pensions have been pegged at a 2% annual increase. They have marched, met with Parliament Portfolio committees and pleaded with their board. Nothing shifts. Today there are only 50 000 left and 14 000 are on full pension their widows some 37 000 live on 70% of the original amount.

Summary:
In 2013 the Pensioners launched the largest class action in the country but it still hasn’t started to be argued in court as Transnet has successfully stalled the process. The case is Claim 1: Pensions to be increased as promised and pensioners to be compensated for arrears. ( Transnet challenged this and the Pensioners took it to the Constitutional Court in November 2017 and a ruling is expected any day)
Claim 2: Transnet to pay the legacy debt of R17Bn plus interest.
CLaim 3: Transnet to repay the R309M illegal donation plus interest to the Transport Pension Fund
20 000 pensioners have died since the start of the case. These pensioner range from train drivers, ticket collectors and firemen to top SAA pilots. The black pensioners don’t receive a pension at all- they got a lump sum pay-out. Top pensions are R24 000 a month, the lowest R1380. After deductions have been made for the medical aid some get as little as R600. 400 pensioners die a year, they fear it’s a waiting game for them all to die and the money returns to Transnet. Allegations of corruption continue, funds continue to go missing. 580 million was invested in Trillion and is yet to be paid back
The fund is run by a board of 8 Trustees and a Chair- the Principle Officer. 4 of the trustees and the Principle officer are all Transnet employees 4 trustees are pensioners and Transnet Second Defined Benefit Fund pensioners and nominated by pensioners to represent them. Currently there is a 4.7 Million surplus in the fund which one Trustee Claire Fichardt is fighting to get paid out to the pensioners while they wait for the outcome of the court case. But Transnet say they need the money to fight the case. The reason there is a surplus is that so many have died and this money remains in the fund and because their pensions have only increased by 2% since 2003. Its a closed fund, Transnet makes no contribution anymore and the pensions say its their hard earned money and they are dying in poverty.

Press Release:


Transnet Pension Funds
For 15 years, desperate Transnet pensioners have been calling for pension increases they could actually live on. By 2013 it had culminated in the country’s largest class action lawsuit, but five years later, the case is yet to be heard. Meanwhile, thousands of pensioners are living below the poverty line with some couples so destitute they’re forced to take turns to eat. Despite protests, court cases and parliamentary recommendations, nothing has changed. Carte Blanche asks: why is nobody paying attention to the plight of these pensioners?


Script:


Script: For the last 27 years Transnet pensioners have been fighting to get what the State promised them, a pension they could live on.
Hennie “We worked day and night I was very seldom at home. I spent most of my time at work to keep Transnet on the go.
Bettie 06 21 14 00 “They couldn’t strike there were no unions they couldn’t go to and say I have been working 18 hours now they are forcing me to go back and work they couldn’t do that
Script: Hennie van der Merwe gave the best years of his life to Transnet, working as a train conductor for 30 years, 5 of them without leave. Today, Bettie and Hennie live on a pension of R1328 a month after medical aid deductions.
05:39 Alfred: When I ask them about our pension, they say it will come. Pension fund will be paid out, you’ll get it.
Script: Alfred Maabu worked for 24 years as a barrier attendant and clerk. In 1990, he received a lump sum pay-out. He’s spent his retirement, fighting for justice alongside his colleagues.
05:22 Alfred: You have to make a plan, get some piece jobs, for us to survive. Transnet has messed with our minds, lots of us sick, others have died
Nap “I was working there 30 years Nap. We've been let down because we were working day and night 24 hours out of 24 hours and you was forced to work overtime because your salary wasn’t much
Script: Nap Ries started out on the steam trains as a fireman and driver, he ended his career driving freight trains. Engines are noisy places and it cost Nap his hearing, forcing him into early retirement from Transnet. They moved in with their children, helping their daughter with her swimming school because his R4000 pension hardly covers the basics.
Pieter “When I was boarded there was no lump sum there was nothing just R100 pension.
Script: Pieter Olivier was a shunter for 30 years until a train derailed and he was trapped under the carriages injuring his back, he was 47 at the time.
Pieter ‘Now it’s R1 500 a month you can’t do anything with that money
Margret 00.31 “Some pensioners really took their own lives. I'm one of those I thought about it.
Link: “This fight started in 2003, when their pensions were pegged at a 2% annual increase, It’s one longest fights for justice by the oldest and arguably weakest members of society and they are literally dying waiting for their day in court. At the onset there were 80 000 pensioners, today there are only 50 000 left and 60% of those are their widows
Script: It started in the 90’s when The South African Transport Services commercialised becoming Transnet, and several different pensions’ schemes were set up through an act in parliament. With no recourse to the Pensions Fund adjudicator, their fate lies in the hands of a board of trustees and Transnet, who in turn answer to parliament. Clair Fichardt, was an SAA pilot for 35 years.
Clair “I've been in a Transnet elected trustee for the last four years each successive chairman has just very successfully fobbed us off .10 57 20 I know that I'm winding my neck out by speaking to you but I'm prepared to take the fall for it. Somebody has got to listen to me and do something from parliamentary level.
Script: After years of trying to change things from within the Fund, Clair broke ranks by speaking to us. The Fund says they don’t have the power to change the rules, and the pensioners feel they are trapped between the Fund, and Parliament.
Clair 10.52 38 “Ever since I became a trustee Lyn Brown has been prevailed upon to sign this to 2% clause, and you know bearing in mind that there are only four trustee meetings a year. It has just been very very successfully fobbed off all the time.
Link: The Pension Fund has been getting the raw end of the deal ever since its inception. It started off with a legacy debt from Transnet of 17. Billion which they promised to pay back over 20 years through bonds
Script: If Transnet had been able to honour it’s commitment to pay the deficit with interest over 20 years then the fund would have been in a far stronger position today. In 2003 The Trustees of the Pension fund released Transnet from its commitment accepting MCell shares and other assests in exchange.
Clair “If and if that had not taken place the fund would have been very strong and we wouldn't have this problem today
Link “When it started out pensioners received 75% cost of living increase over and above their 2% that all changed in 2003 when the fund said they were not obliged to pay this, the pensioners were then forced to survive only on their pension
Alfred: It’s hard man, some of these guys are being moved into shacks and out of the house. You end up sleeping outside, others make a plan. Others it’s just the wife who works and they are living from hand to mouth. 02:09:12
Bettie “In the morning we have some coffee and some sandwiches we skip lunchtime and in the evenings, we can’t afford meat.
Script: Bettie has a washing machine and a stove but she can’t afford the electricity to run them. She makes ends meet by doing part time legal work
Bettie”. I mean I must go into the office and I must work .., time is running out …its not fair , it’s not fair ……
Nap “So now with a 2 percent increase in a year I get R82 with R82 and I can do absolutely. So you're going backwards instead of forwards.
Mac is there anyone you have spoken to at Transnet
Margret “They are not interested do talk to you. That's why I write Lyn Brown with emails. I write to Pravin Gordhan and I write to Ramaphosa now and there is no comeback.
Script: They feel like a political football. In 2011 Parliament recommended they get 3.2 % increase annually, and 75% cost of living increase back dated to 2000, nothing happened. Transnet CEO at the time, Brian Molefe, promised R1.9 Billion to the pension fund- but it all came to naught.
Realising they were completely on their own, the pensioners formed The Transnet Pensioners Action Group and started to sue Transnet and the Fund, approaching Wynanda Coetzee as their advocate
Wynanda “first claim is that there was a state promise that the Transnet workers that they will get at least 2 percent annual increase but it will be as in the past higher approximately 70 percent of inflation and that obviously didn't happen.
Link: In 2013 they launched the largest class action case in the history of South Africa but it’s yet to be argued in court. Transnet and the Fund has opposed it every step of the way.
Script: Finally there was some light at the end of the tunnel. Just recently the Constitutional Court upheld their appeal, and ruled that all their claims had merit. Now the case can now be argued, probably starting next year and running for several years.
Pieter “They are just going to let the case go on and on and on they are just taking us as fools
Clair. The feeling out there amongst the pensioners is that Transnet is holding up until the last man standing dies and they can pocket a lot of money.
Script: Currently, there is a 4.7 Billion surplus in the pension fund, which Clair wants to pay out to the pensioners while they wait for the court case to be resolved.
Clair “ I'm looking for a way under the present rules where we can dispose of the surplus and it is within the power of the board to do so. Whereas they are looking at ways to which require ministerial intervention.
Script: It was time to get some answers.
Mac on the phone. “Good evening Mr Maritz we would like to do an interview”
Peet” We are not interested in taking part in the programme”
Script: Transnet had declined an interview asking us to speak to Peet Maritz the presiding officer for the Fund. But Peet had refused to speak to us for weeks.
Link: So we are at the Transnet Pension Fund officers on the 13th floor we are trying to get hold of Mr Peet Maritz he doesn’t answer calls he doesn’t answer emails even when we called him he said he didn’t want to be part of the program.
Script: Finally he relented, speaking to the media for the first time in years.
Mac- The pensioners believe the process is being stalled deliberately and you waiting for them to die
Peet “I think it's really absurd statement to make that anyone is waiting for the demise of the pensioners. We have ask the representatives of the pensioners to withdraw the pension funds from this litigation but they persist
Mac “This has been going on since 2011 why not just pay them”
Peet “ I think it will be ill advised to anyone in the light of a possible claim of 80 billion rand like that to start paying out the surpluses acquired by the fund. And one needs that money to maintain the liquidity in the fund and to be able to honour the pension obligations of the fund towards the pensioners
Mac Why is the pension fund being sued and not just Transnet
Wynanda “the pension funds need to make the payments to the pensioners. And that's why they are a party to this action
Mac “The pensions believe that their own money is being used to fight against them
Peet “That is a totally wrong perception because there is no assets of the pension fund being used to fight the litigation, the funds is from the operational budget is funded by Transnet
Clair “Peet Maritz is the fly in the ointment as far as we are concerned. He stands between us and the surplus as such and every move we make is blocked by him. Peet Maritz is the one and only person that I can blame directly for the present situation
Peet “ I don't have any vote or say in the way the pensions are being paid or of the benefit structure is being developed. It's a function of the fiduciary duties of the board of trustees with the approval of and concurrence of the various state departments in this regard.
Script “The Fund says they can’t change the rules it’s up to parliament, and parliament hasn’t made any moves to change them in 15 years.
Clair “All I can say to Pravin Gordhan is that I hope that you can sort out this mess.
Script: And the pensioners despair, as Transnet squanders money on things like 18 breakfast sessions costing over R17 million. Many have lost hope of ever seeing their money, even if they win their court case.
Margret “You feel desperate. I feel like a beggar. I really feel like a beggar. If Transnet was supposed to pay us like they should then it wasn’t necessary
Alfred: I’ve been angry for many years that but I’ve accepted now. We were hoping that when the case comes, we would be successful because we expected them to be on Transnet necks.
Bettie “As long as there is still a breath in my life I will fight I will fight Transnet I will fight the trustees with every power I have got, this is murder this is its dam well murdering us
Script: But for Bettie, Alfred, and all the 1000s of pensioners, maybe there is a glimmer of hope from the last thing Peet Maritz told us
Peet “ There is discussions around trying to settle this case and not go one with the litigation and settle the matter you know that is on the go .

metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is a fight that has been going on since 2003 and it’s a fight by the oldest and arguably weakest members of society- some 80 000 Transnet Pensioners. Many worked all their lives for the company and believed their old age was secure as the pension fund was arguably one of the strongest at the time. But it got plundered by the State, funds borrowed and not returned, bonds not repaid and since 2003 their pensions have been pegged at a 2% annual increase. They have marched, met with Parliament Portfolio committees and pleaded with their board. Nothing shifts. Today there are only 50 000 left and 14 000 are on full pension their widows some 37 000 live on 70% of the original amount.
metadata.Summary: In 2013 the Pensioners launched the largest class action in the country but it still hasn’t started to be argued in court as Transnet has successfully stalled the process. The case is Claim 1: Pensions to be increased as promised and pensioners to be compensated for arrears. ( Transnet challenged this and the Pensioners took it to the Constitutional Court in November 2017 and a ruling is expected any day) Claim 2: Transnet to pay the legacy debt of R17Bn plus interest. CLaim 3: Transnet to repay the R309M illegal donation plus interest to the Transport Pension Fund 20 000 pensioners have died since the start of the case. These pensioner range from train drivers, ticket collectors and firemen to top SAA pilots. The black pensioners don’t receive a pension at all- they got a lump sum pay-out. Top pensions are R24 000 a month, the lowest R1380. After deductions have been made for the medical aid some get as little as R600. 400 pensioners die a year, they fear it’s a waiting game for them all to die and the money returns to Transnet. Allegations of corruption continue, funds continue to go missing. 580 million was invested in Trillion and is yet to be paid back The fund is run by a board of 8 Trustees and a Chair- the Principle Officer. 4 of the trustees and the Principle officer are all Transnet employees 4 trustees are pensioners and Transnet Second Defined Benefit Fund pensioners and nominated by pensioners to represent them. Currently there is a 4.7 Million surplus in the fund which one Trustee Claire Fichardt is fighting to get paid out to the pensioners while they wait for the outcome of the court case. But Transnet say they need the money to fight the case. The reason there is a surplus is that so many have died and this money remains in the fund and because their pensions have only increased by 2% since 2003. Its a closed fund, Transnet makes no contribution anymore and the pensions say its their hard earned money and they are dying in poverty.
